m2c/tests/headless/headless_rig.py -- Patch C10: the shared rig of the headless-mode tests.

Why this is a plain module and not a conftest.py: tests/test_doctor.py does ``from conftest import ...``,
which resolves by module name, and a second conftest.py in tests/headless would shadow the real one (the
same reason tests/auth/auth_fixtures.py and tests/link/link_fakes.py exist).  Each test file imports what
it needs from here.

WHAT IS REUSED.  The fake device server of C04 (tests/link/link_fakes.py): a real ``websockets`` server on
127.0.0.1 whose per-connection scripts decide exactly what the "server" says.  This module adds, on top of it:

    ThreadedServer     runs that fake server in a thread of its own, so a test can call the SYNCHRONOUS
                       ``cli.main([...])`` / ``headless.run_headless(...)`` (which start their own event
                       loop with ``asyncio.run``) against it, with the real DeviceLink in between.
    Stream / scripted  a tiny model of the server's side of one run: it numbers the stream (seq 1, 2, 3...)
                       and says ``created`` after run.start and ``running`` after the user_message, the
                       order protocol/fixtures/*.jsonl pin; a test supplies only what happens next.
    call_headless      ``run_headless`` with StringIO streams and fast link options.
    run_cli            ``cli.main`` with capsys, signed in against a ThreadedServer.

Every client message the fake server receives is validated

m2c/tests/headless/test_headless_process.py -- Patch C10: Ctrl-C and SIGTERM, and the command line itself.

The signal tests run the REAL program as a child process (a signal cannot be tested honestly in-process) against the
C04 fake server in this process's thread, and watch what the server receives: a ``cancel`` for the run, then a normal
close.  The child must exit non-zero (130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM, the shell conventions) without a traceback, and in
json mode it must still leave exactly one JSON object on stdout.

The second half is the surface in cli.py: ``-p/--print``, ``--output-format``, ``--mode``, ``m2c --help`` documenting the
exit codes, and every existing command still working next to them.

m2c/tests/headless/test_headless_tools.py -- Patch C10: the non-interactive policy and the injected tool hooks.

headless.py defines two small injected interfaces -- ``decide(proposal)`` and ``execute(proposal)`` -- because the
policy engine (C06) and the tool executors (C05) are built in parallel and are not on this base; the integration
patch (I02) wires the real ones in.  These tests pin the contract the later patch relies on:

  * only an explicit ``allow`` runs a tool; ``ask``, ``deny``, an exception, a malformed answer, a missing policy
    and a missing executor all fail the run as a policy denial (exit 3), failing closed;
  * the denial is reported first, as ``approval{call_id, decision: deny, scope: once}`` and with no
    ``tool_result`` (P00: a denied call gets an approval and no tool_result), and only then is the run cancelled;
  * an allowed call is answered with a ``tool_result`` alone (P00 fixture 02: auto-allowed calls need no approval).

m2c/tests/headless/test_headless_wiring.py -- Patch C10b: ``m2c -p`` runs tools for real, under a policy nobody can answer.

Every test drives the real CLI (``cli.main``) or ``headless.run_headless`` against C04's fake server in a thread and a
temporary project folder.  The tool runner, the policy engine, the shell tool, the checkpoints and the store are the real
ones; only the server and the keyring are fakes.  What is NOT covered here, and why:

* the real bubblewrap sandbox (no ``bwrap`` on the machine this patch was written on): the sandbox modes are tested with
  the suite's "no working sandbox" status and with a counting stand-in for the probe;
* SIGTERM and SIGINT, which need a real child process: test_headless_wiring_process.py.

m2c/tests/headless/test_headless_wiring_process.py -- Patch C10b: Ctrl-C and SIGTERM while a command is running.

The real ``m2c -p`` in a child process, the fake server in a thread, and a real ``sleep`` as the long-running command.
When the signal arrives the child must: kill the command (not leave it running), tell the server ``cancel``, exit
non-zero (143 for SIGTERM, 130 for SIGINT, the shell conventions) without a traceback, and never send a tool_result for
the command it killed.  ``--sandbox off`` keeps the child independent of whether bubblewrap is installed here.

m2c/tests/headless/wiring_rig.py -- Patch C10b: what the "headless runs really use tools" tests share.

A plain module (not a conftest) for the same reason headless_rig.py is one: other test directories import from it.
It adds to the C10 rig (``headless_rig``: the fake server in a thread, ``run_cli``, ``call_headless``):

``steps_tail``      a server script that proposes tool calls one after the other, the way the real agent loop does,
                    and says what it expects back for each (a ``tool_result`` when the device ran it, an ``approval``
                    when the device refused it), then gives a final reply when every call was answered.
``network_guard``   a fixture that fails the test if anything connects anywhere but the loopback fake server.
``make_setup``      the ``tool_setup`` argument of ``run_headless`` for a project folder, built the way the CLI builds it.
``tool_results``    the ``tool_result`` payloads the server received, by call id.
``checkpoint_rows`` the rows of the store's ``checkpoints`` table, for one session.

No literal in this file looks like a credential; tests that need a fake secret build it at run time.
